name: Perplexity
tagline: AI answer engine with web search, citations, and research modes

pricing.notes: Official pages checked 2026-07-30; Pro listed at $20/month or $200/year.

verdictSummary: A retrieval-plus-LLM answer engine is buildable, but Perplexity's search stack, source ranking, UX, mobile/browser surfaces, and model access make full parity hard.
coreLoopDIY: Search the web/API, fetch pages, rank passages, ask an LLM to answer with citations, and store threads.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because answers arrive fast with sources and fewer query-building chores.

priorArt.name: Perplexica
priorArt.desc: Open-source AI search engine inspired by Perplexity.

alternatives.name: GPT Researcher
alternatives.desc: A research agent rather than a search box; it returns cited reports and a bill from whichever model you chose.

alternatives.name: Khoj
alternatives.desc: A personal AI that searches the web and your files; broader than Perplexity, and noticeably heavier to run.

alternatives.name: Local Deep Research
alternatives.desc: Less search box, more research intern: it searches, iterates and writes cited reports on your own hardware.

alternatives.name: Morphic
alternatives.desc: A cited answer engine with a prettier face; Docker quietly brings PostgreSQL, Redis and SearXNG along.

alternatives.name: Vane
alternatives.desc: Perplexity with the meter removed: cited answers and deep research, provided you can run one Docker stack.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Perplexity Standard
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Basic searches are practically unlimited; Pro Search and Research are explicitly very limited, which is the paid product's point.

notes: A nuanced kinda: there is real open-source prior art, but source quality and scale matter.
prompt:
Build me a personal answer engine like Perplexity, wrapping real search and LLM APIs,
not rebuilding them. Requirements:

- A local web app on localhost:3000: Node + Express + htmx, one input box, streamed
  answers.
- Per question: query the Brave Search API (key in .env), fetch the top 6 results with
  undici, extract readable text with @mozilla/readability + jsdom, then pass the
  question plus numbered excerpts to Claude or GPT (key in .env) with instructions to
  answer only from the excerpts and cite as [1][2].
- Render citations as footnote links; show the full source list under every answer.
- Follow-up questions stay in the same thread with prior Q&A in the context window.
- Threads stored in SQLite via better-sqlite3; a sidebar lists past threads by first
  question.
- If a page fails to fetch or extract, drop it and continue. Never cite a page that was
  not fetched.
- Binds to localhost only; no accounts, no telemetry, only the search and LLM calls
  leave my machine.
- Out of scope: crawling my own web index, model routing, and mobile apps. Answer
  quality tracks the search API, that is the deal.
- README: which keys to get (Brave Search has a free tier) and rough per-query cost.
